messages:
Mike (infra): Quick sync — ran the Q3 hosted API procurement sims this morning. TL;DR: baseline + seasonal = ~1.8M GPU-hours. Need to choose buy/lease/rent mix. Thoughts?
Anya (capacity): Can you paste the key outputs? short numbers are fine.
Mike (infra): Pasting top-level sim snapshot:
```
scenario: mid_p50
q3_gpu_hours_needed: 1_800_000
avg_utilization: 0.72
95p_peak_hour_block: 220_000
cost_buy_per_gpu_hr: $0.35
cost_lease_per_gpu_hr: $0.48
breakeven_months_if_bought_vs_lease: 9
```
Anya (capacity): ok. That breakeven looks reasonable. My initial recommendation: buy ~40% of steady-state demand, lease ~40% for committed burst capacity, keep ~20% for short-term rentals / warm-pool. Preserves flexibility and reduces opex shock.
Ben (finance): 40% buy implies ~ $3.6M capex hit this quarter (rough calc). Lease OPEX would be ~ $1.2M/quarter. Need CFO signoff if capex > $2M.
Shiv (ops): Important: APAC suppliers are still 10-12 week lead time for discrete buys. If we rely on buys for APAC peak we're exposed. Recommend leases in APAC, buys in US/EU where lead times shorter.
Linda (sre): Also callout: if we over-buy a single SKU, our fallback options shrink. Want to keep headroom for quantized models on mixed hardware. Add a min-compatibility constraint to the procurement RFQ.
Mike (infra): Good point. Also thinking autoscale policy: prefer burst to leased pool first, then short-term rentals. Cap max burst to rented pool at 30% of total fleet to avoid cost runaway. Thoughts?
Anya (capacity): sounds fine. I'll run sensitivity: 30% burst cap vs 50% and post delta on cost/availability. Also propose commit windows: buys: 6-9 month ramp (staggered), leases: 9-12 month terms, rentals fill spike windows.
Ben (finance): We should model cashflow: front-loaded capex vs smoother lease opex. If cash is tight, push more to leases even if unit cost higher. Need scenario with 20/60/20 split.
Shiv (ops): On network/region constraints: egress capacity in EU-west is slightly degraded during peak tests — might need to provision small additional NAT/egress capacity with new racks. Otherwise hotspots will throttle throughput, not GPU compute.
Mike (infra): Good catch — include network egress provisioning as part of procurement order (power + network).
FleetBot: deployment-sim finished: canary pass rate 98.6%, warm-pool cold-start median 4.3s, KV cache warm fraction 0.67.
Linda (sre): For SLAs: propose we reserve 5% of committed capacity for canaries and emergency fallbacks. That reduces usable capacity but protects reliability.
Anya (capacity): Agreed. I'll fold that into the model (adds ~90k GPU-hours to buffer in Q3).
Mike (infra): Next concrete steps: 1) finalize region split by EOD Friday (who owns region mapping?), 2) @Ben produce capex ask + cashflow scenarios by Monday, 3) Procurement to RFP for 12mo leases and 6-9mo buy quotes.
Ben (finance): I'll get the capex vs lease scenarios together. Need procurement numbers from you @Mike and vendor lead times from @Shiv.
Shiv (ops): I'll pull vendor lead-time matrix and APAC lease vendor shortlist.
Linda (sre): I'll draft the fallback/runbook adjustments and the 5% canary reservation.
Anya (capacity): I'll post the spreadsheet + sensitivity sims (20/60/20, 40/40/20, 60/20/20) and include the buffer.
Mike (infra): Awesome. If we can converge on region split by Friday I can start procurement outreach. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Ben (finance): ack :money_with_wings: 
Mike (infra): tagging @Anya @Ben @Shiv for action items.
